LanguageData.Dominion_Bloc_Hawks_Desc: Favour war and expansion. Grow during wars and with aggressive leaders.
LanguageData.Dominion_Bloc_Doves_Desc: Favour peace. Grow with war weariness and push for ceasefires.
LanguageData.Dominion_Bloc_Merchants_Desc: Favour trade and stable relations. Grow with a strong economy and greedy leaders.
LanguageData.Dominion_Bloc_Zealots_Desc: Put the faith first. Strong in religious and proselytising ideologies.
LanguageData.Dominion_Bloc_Reformists_Desc: Want the system changed. Grow when stability and legitimacy are low, and weaken stability.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_AiDiplomacy_Desc: AI factions declare war, make peace, ally and break alliances with each other on their own. Your own relations are never changed by this.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_PoliticalEvents_Desc: Unstable factions can suffer riots, coups and revolutions. Revolutions change a faction's government and leader; factions are never split.

LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_FalseRumors_Desc: Little-known factions attract baseless rumours, reported as unconfirmed. They are corrected once you learn enough about the faction.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_NewsThoughts_Desc: Wars and unrest near the colony, peace, and attacks on allies affect your colonists' mood.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_LetterForMajor_Desc: Major news (wars, coups, revolutions, lost capitals, broken treaties, Federation news and other major events) arrives as a letter even in categories set to Message.

LanguageData.Dominion_Dip_Influence_Desc: Influence is spent on diplomacy. Your head of state earns it by working at the Leadership Desk (statecraft work).

LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_CommonGround_De: Talk about what your peoples share. Better with a skilled speaker and a similar ideology.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_CommonGround: {0} speaks of the interests your peoples share.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_CommonGround_Success: {0} nods slowly. "There is truth in that."
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_Flattery_Desc: Praise their leader and their people. Paranoid leaders see through it.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_Concession_Desc: Give something up front: 300 silver, or 10 influence if you lack the silver. Greedy leaders love it.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Concession: {0} makes a gesture of goodwill and puts a gift on the table.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Concession_Success: {0} accepts the gift with evident pleasure.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Concession_Fail: {0} accepts the gift, but only out of courtesy.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_Threat_Desc: Make clear what happens if they refuse. Works only if you are about as strong as them or stronger; honourable leaders resent it.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Threat: {0} reminds them, coldly, of your strength.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Threat_Success: {0} goes pale and becomes far more accommodating.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Threat_Fail: {0} stands up, furious. "You dare threaten us at this table?"
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_Apology_Desc: Acknowledge their grievances. Honourable leaders value it, and their grievances shrink.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Apology: {0} acknowledges the wrongs of the past.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Apology_Fail: {0} waves it away. "Too little, too late."
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_Leverage_Desc: Remind them that you hold some of their people. Effective, but the honourable call it blackmail.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Leverage: {0} mentions, almost in passing, the prisoners you hold.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Leverage_Success: {0} understands perfectly and softens their stance.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_SharedEnemies_D: Remind them of the enemies you share.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_SharedEnemies: {0} raises the threat you both face.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_SharedEnemies_Fail: {0} shrugs. "Our enemies are our own business."
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_IdeologyAppeal_: Speak of the faith and values you have in common.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_IdeologyAppeal: {0} speaks of the beliefs your peoples share.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_IdeologyAppeal_Succe: {0} warms to you. "We understand each other."
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_IdeologyAppeal_Fail: {0} disagrees on the finer points, at length.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMoveLabel_Candour_Desc: Be completely honest, even where it hurts. Honourable leaders respect it.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitMove_Candour: {0} lays out your position without any embellishment.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitIncident_0: A protester breaks into the hall, shouting, and has to be dragged out. The mood sours.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitIncident_1: A messenger hurries in with news for {0}. Whatever it is, it changes the mood.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitIncident_2: Guards foil a plot against the summit. The shared danger draws both sides closer.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitIncident_3: An interpreter mangles a key phrase, and it takes a while to clear up the misunderstanding.
LanguageData.Dominion_SummitIncident_4: A shared meal between rounds goes well. Even {0} laughs once.

LanguageData.Dominion_Federation_Rules: A major faction is unified when it joins the Federation (sign Federation membership by comms, envoy or summit), when you hold at least as many of its settlements as vassal outposts as it has left (and, once it is gone, at least half of what it once had), or when it falls while at war with you after you have beaten one of its settlements in battle.

LanguageData.Dominion_Federation_CharterText: The Rim Council has adopted the Federation Charter. Any major faction may now sign Federation membership with you, through the comms console, an envoy or a summit. Friends may also ask to join on their own.
LanguageData.Dominion_Federation_NoCharter: needs the Federation Charter in force
LanguageData.Dominion_UnifyStatus_None_Desc: Not yet unified. Raise their opinion of you and offer Federation membership, take their settlements as vassal outposts, or defeat them.
LanguageData.Dominion_UnifyStatus_Federation_Desc: Signed Federation membership. A member who comes to dislike you may leave.
LanguageData.Dominion_UnifyStatus_Subjugated_Desc: You hold at least as many of their former settlements as vassal outposts as they have left.
LanguageData.Dominion_UnifyStatus_Conquered_Desc: Fell while at war with you, after you defeated one of their settlements yourself.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ending_Intro:
The Federation of {0}
{1} peoples now stand under one banner: {2} who joined freely, {3} who were made vassals, {4} who were conquered.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ending_Federation: It was built with words, not walls. Summit by summit and treaty by treaty, {1} convinced the rival powers that they were stronger together than apart. The Rim Council became a parliament, and the old borders became lines on a map that no one patrols any more.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ending_Subjugated: It was built on obligation. One settlement at a time, {0} took the old powers under its protection until there was no one left to resist. The vassals pay their dues and keep their peace, and if they grumble, they grumble quietly.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ending_Conquered: It was built by the sword. The rival powers that would not bend were broken, and {1} rules what remains. Order has come to the planet; whether it is loved is another matter.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ending_Mixed: It was built every way there was: some peoples signed the charter willingly, some were bound as vassals, and some were defeated. {1} learned to use every tool, and in the end the planet answers to {0}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ending_Outro: The story of the colony goes on, but the age of feuding powers is over.
